Subject: Draft MAP + sprint canvas — HelioMed pilot (initial)

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Thanks again for the sync this morning. As discussed, I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) tailored for the pilot scope we sketched (document stub + a one-page sprint canvas). The goal here is to capture the 30–45 day acceptance path, stakeholders, and the handful of legal/ops questions we need to clear before we lock a kickoff date.

High-level asks from our side:
- Review the MAP doc and add/edit the stakeholder owners (column on the right).
- Confirm procurement timing for onboarding (we listed "standard PO + SOW" as the expected route).
- Share the right point of contact for SOC2 / security evidence (we can send the questionnaire).

Proposed timeline (editable on the doc):
Week 0: Kickoff + environment provisioning (Redwood private trial cluster)
Week 1–2: Integration + sample data tests (embedding/LLM prompts)
Week 3–4: Acceptance testing with 3 core workflows
Go/No-go: Stakeholder review and acceptance sign-off

I also added a short list of items for Legal / Procurement under the "Ops/Legal asks" section — Tom, please review and let us know if anything is missing.

Attachments: HelioMed_MAP_draft.gdoc (link below), week0-sprint-canvas.png, pricing-ops-stub.pdf

Docs: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HelioMapDraft
HubSpot deal: hs:deal:2381745

If that looks okay, can we lock a kickoff for the week of July 5? I put a couple times in the doc for a 60‑minute alignment workshop.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Thanks Kimberly — this is helpful and much appreciated.

Quick notes after a first pass:
- The stakeholder matrix looks right but I need to swap one of the owners (Clinical Ops should own the acceptance checklist, not Product). I added a comment on the doc.
- Procurement: we typically route smaller pilots via a PO; SOW is required for anything that touches PHI. For this pilot we will need a minimal SOW addendum — I flagged procurement (Tom) to confirm.
- Security evidence: contact for SOC2 and data flow is frank.li@heliomed.com (he's cc'd on this thread in a separate email thread we'll forward).

Regarding timing, July 5 works for a kickoff in principle but I need to confirm that our infra team can provision test infra by then. I should have a firm answer by EOD tomorrow.

A few logistical asks from our side: can you add a short acceptance test script example for the three workflows (we need something our QA can execute against your trial)? Also include token usage expectations — our finance team wants a rough cost estimate for the trial period.

Best,
Alicia
Director, Partnerships
HelioMed Systems
agomez@heliomed.com

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Draft MAP + sprint canvas — HelioMed pilot (initial)

Alicia — thanks for the quick review and the procurement note. A few follow-ups inline and next steps:

1) Ownership swap: thanks — I accepted your comment and moved Clinical Ops into the acceptance owner column.

2) Acceptance test scripts: Marissa has added a short checklist for the three acceptance workflows (happy path prompts, expected metrics, and a minimal test harness description). See the new "Acceptance Examples" section in the doc. Marissa — can you confirm the test steps are runnable by HelioMed QA without infra changes?

3) Token usage / cost: Jonas attached a short stubbed pricing note in the attachments (pricing-ops-stub.pdf). This is a conservative estimate for the trial (batching enabled, KV cache configured). Jonas — if they opt for more heavy inference sampling we can update the estimate; can you add a one-paragraph note on how batching/kv caching reduces cost?

4) Legal / SOW: Tom — appreciate you checking on the SOW requirement. If PHI is involved we'll scope and propose a minimal addendum; otherwise a PO should suffice.

5) Workshop: I'll leave two slots in the doc for Wednesday July 7 and Friday July 9; if July 5 becomes possible we can move earlier.

Next: I'll incorporate Marissa/Jonas updates to the doc and send a clean link once that's done (target: Thu EOD).

Thanks —
Kim

Hi all —

Quick confirmation from Engineering/CS side: the acceptance examples are intentionally lightweight — three smoke tests (1) patient lookup + summarization, (2) automated triage suggestions, (3) record-matching for duplicate detection. Each test includes: input sample, expected output criteria (precision/recall thresholds), and a basic end-to-end checklist.

For HelioMed QA: these run against the trial endpoint without infra changes. If you prefer an on-prem validation we'll scope that separately (it adds ~1 week).

Jonas — I left a note in the pricing stub that explains batching and KV cache behavior and how it affects token burn.

Happy to hop on the alignment workshop to walk through the acceptance scenarios.

-M
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference
